battle.name: 隋平楊諒之戰
battle.brief: 開皇四年（604）末，隋文帝崩，楊廣即位，其弟秦王楊諒以并州為基地舉兵，眾至十餘萬；關中一路由韋雲起襲虎牢，河北一路由王世充掃平諸城。十一月戰於鞏縣淵水，叛軍夜潰，楊諒與數十人奔城陽，為追騎擒送洛陽。卡面科林斯青銅盔非本役實物，正可對照隋軍兜鍪與輕騎機動作戰的取向。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 這場戰爭是隋朝開國初期的一場宗室內亂。起兵的一方是秦王楊諒，據並州（太原）為基地，活動區在河北；他拒不接受新君的詔書，遣使請罪而不見寬宥，遂自稱丞相、仍署並州總管，聚眾而反。叛軍並非編制完整的國軍，而是楊諒在中軍之外臨時徵集的河北各州郡鄉兵、流亡亡命與無應募者，器械不齊、指揮不一，據城而守與野戰混雜；楊諒又遣使結好突厥始畢可汗，約為外援，但北方之兵並未真正參戰。另一方是隋中央朝廷：兵馬由剛即位的隋主楊廣直接調度，以行軍總管分統兩路——關中一路由韋雲起領精騎出潼關、逾崤函，負責襲取虎牢、斷楊諒西路；河南一路以王世充為河南道行軍總管，率諸軍自洛陽一線掃平河北諸城，兩軍最後會師於鞏縣淵水。隋軍骨幹是關中宿衛與府兵，裝備與操練較整齊，糧食由洛陽倉儲及河南州郡供應，朝廷為籌軍資還一度蠲免河南部分租賦。第三方是突厥：始畢可汗遣使往還、口頭上給了楊諒指望，真正決定戰局的仍是關中與河南兩支隋軍。
countriesEn: This conflict was a princely civil war in the early years of the Sui dynasty. The side that rose in arms was the Prince of Qin, Yang Liang, whose base was Bingzhou (modern Taiyuan) and whose operations were centred on the Hebei plain. Refusing the new sovereign's summons, he sent envoys to confess his fault but was not pardoned, and then proclaimed himself chancellor while still styling himself as the Bingzhou commander, and gathered a host to revolt. His rebel force was not a properly organised state army: apart from Yang Liang's own central command it consisted of militia levies hastily drawn from the prefectures and counties of Hebei, of fugitives and of men who had answered no call at all. Its equipment was uneven, its command structure divided, and it mixed the holding of towns with field operations. Yang Liang also sent envoys to the Türkish Qaghan, Ashina Shibi, to solicit foreign help, but no Turkic troops actually took part. The other side was the Sui court itself: the troops were directed by the newly enthroned Emperor Yang Guang, who split them between two lines under the office of xingjun zongguan, commander-in-chief of an expeditionary force. The Guanzhong line was led by Wei Yunqi, who took the elite cavalry out beyond Tongguan and the Hangu passes to strike at Hulao and cut off Yang Liang's western flank. The Henan line was led by Wang Shichong, appointed commander of the Henan circuit, who swept the cities of Hebei with the various armies drawn from the Luoyang region, and the two lines finally met at Yuanshui near Gongxian. The backbone of the Sui force was the imperial guards of Guanzhong together with the fubing militia, whose equipment and drill were regular, while the grain came from the depots of Luoyang and the prefectures of Henan; the court even remitted part of the land tax of Henan to keep the army supplied. The third party was the Türkish steppe: Shibi Qaghan sent envoys back and forth and gave Yang Liang verbal encouragement, but what actually decided the war was the two Sui columns from Guanzhong and from Henan.
people: 關鍵人物都在隋室宗親與其將領之間。開皇四年（604）七月文帝崩、楊廣即位，兩個月後就遇上弟弟的挑戰；這位新君是本役的決策者，他不接受楊諒的請罪與求和，先遣韋雲起斷其西路，再以王世充為主力掃平河北，十一月督軍至洛陽一線，把一場兄弟反目打成鞏固皇位的必要之戰。楊諒是秦王，自幼出鎮並州總管，掌河北兵柄，與楊廣同為獨孤氏所出，兄弟情誼與政治利益本不可分；文帝晚年廢太子楊勇、立晉王楊廣，又屢責諸子奢縱，楊諒與益州王楊秀、襄王楊俊各自握著一方兵權，心中早已積怨。文帝病重時召諸子入宮侍疾，楊諒與楊秀卻逗留在外不得入，猜疑由此加深；起兵後他自為都督、統中軍，屢遣使請和不許，最後在淵水戰敗，偽遣使請降實欲北走突厥，為追騎所擒，削爵為庶人，幽於益州，至大業十年（614）卒於蜀地，年五十有四。將領方面，關中一路主將韋雲起以輕兵掩其不意襲破虎牢、設疑兵破敵於陝縣側翼，十數日而定關中，兵不血刃地切斷了楊諒西進的通道；河南道行軍總管王世充統諸軍與楊諒戰於淵水，乘其疲弊夜擊，一戰而潰其眾，又親率追騎擒楊諒，是本役首功。《隋書》另記楊素與高熲曾奉詔赴洛陽商討討諒方略，當時楊素方鎮揚州，謀議雖見於記載，實際戰線仍由韋、王二人執行。
peopleEn: The decisive figures are all members of the imperial clan of the Sui and their commanders. In the seventh month of 604, the year 604, Emperor Wen died and Yang Guang took the throne; two months later he faced his brother's challenge. The new sovereign was the decision-maker of this campaign: he refused Yang Liang's confession and his offers of peace, first sending Wei Yunqi to sever his western flank, then committing Wang Shichong as the main force to sweep Hebei, and in the eleventh month taking command in the Luoyang area, so that a quarrel between brothers was turned into a necessary war for the consolidation of the throne. Yang Liang was Prince of Qin, had been stationed at Bingzhou as commander from childhood and held the military authority of Hebei, and was a full brother of Yang Guang by the same mother, the Empress Dugu; the tie of brotherhood and the claims of political interest had never been separable in his case. In his last years Emperor Wen deposed the heir, Yang Yong, and installed the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, while repeatedly reproaching his sons for extravagance; Yang Liang, the Prince of Yizhou, Yang Xiu, and the Prince of Xiang, Yang Jun, each commanded troops in a different quarter and had long stored up grievances. When Emperor Wen lay dying and summoned his sons to the palace, Yang Liang and Yang Xiu delayed outside and were not admitted, and the suspicion deepened. After raising his banner Yang Liang made himself commander-in-chief, held the central command, sent envors to sue for peace and was refused, was finally beaten at Yuanshui, sent a false envoy to offer submission in the hope of reaching the Türkish steppe, was caught by the pursuing cavalry, stripped of his title and reduced to commoner status, and was imprisoned in Yizhou until his death there in the tenth year of the Daye era, 614, at the age of fifty-four. Among the commanders, Wei Yunqi of the Guanzhong column surprised Hulao with light troops, turned the enemy at the flank of Shanxian with false dispositions, and settled Guanzhong in a dozen days or so, cutting the road by which Yang Liang might have advanced westward. Wang Shichong, commander of the Henan circuit, fought Yang Liang at Yuanshui with the several armies under him, struck by night when the rebels were worn out, scattered their host in a single action, and then led the pursuing cavalry himself to take Yang Liang prisoner, which made him the leading figure of the campaign. The History of Sui also records that Yang Su and Gao Jiong were summoned to Luoyang to deliberate on the plan for dealing with Yang Liang; Yang Su was then stationed at Yangzhou, and although the deliberations are preserved, the fighting was carried out by Wei and Wang.
kits: 卡面是科林斯青銅盔：全正面開眼、只在鼻樑與眼孔之間留空的希臘式青銅頭盔，盛行於公元前七世紀中葉，到本役開打時早已退出軍備一千兩百年，是一件象徵性的對照件，而不是隋軍頭上真戴的東西。它的形制教訓很清楚：深筒盔身包住頭顱兩側與後頸，只留一條窄縫供雙眼視物，戴上它的人幾乎只能靠腳下的隊形判斷方向，開闊的代價是獨立行動能力的喪失。隋軍這邊的頭盔叫兜鍪、冑，承襲北周以來形制，兩耳下垂護住頸側，披膊護住肩臂，視野與聽覺都更開闊，因此可以縱隊奔馳、各自應變，不必死守腳下的位置。真正上陣的隋軍裝備包括明光鎧這類以金屬片綴連的胸背甲與札葉甲的玄鎧，身上的兩當、蔽膝與長櫜，腰佩橫刀與環首刀，手持長槊（步槊與馬槊），射手用弓、臂弩與蹶張弩配箭，騎兵多披甲馬甲、用槊與刀，軍中另備輜重車、帳幕、鼓與鈦角、旌旗麾幟。隋書記載的攻城器物在本役只是背景而非現場：雲梯、攻城車、撞車、飛雲與巢車都是隋軍平陳時已用過的器械，本役只在據城與野戰之間往復，沒有留下大規模攻城戰的記載。馬匹既是騎兵的底子，也是輜重與鼓吹的來源，與西部邊鎮交涉所得的良馬同樣被朝廷視為要緊。
kitsEn: The card shows a Corinthian helmet: a Greek bronze helmet with the whole face closed in, leaving only a gap for the nose and the eyes. It was fashionable in the middle of the seventh century BC and had left the armoury more than twelve hundred years before this war was fought, so it is a symbolic reference piece rather than anything actually worn by the Sui soldiers. Its lesson is plain: the deep bowl encloses both sides of the head and the nape, leaving only a narrow slot through which the eyes can look, and the man who wears it can judge his bearings only from the formation under his feet. The price of that wide view is the loss of the power to act independently. The Sui helmet was called the doumou or zhou, descended in form from the Northern Zhou, with cheek pieces hanging down to protect the sides of the neck and shoulder guards protecting the upper arms; the field of view and the hearing are both freer, so the troops could move in column and react for themselves instead of being pinned to a fixed place in the line. The equipment the Sui really fought in included breast and back armour of the bright-blaze type, built of metal plates riveted together, and the plated dark armour; on the body a short jacket, knee guards and a long bow case; at the waist a straight sword and a ring-pommelled sword; in the hands a long spear, both the foot variant and the mounted variant; archers with bows, arm crossbows and springald-style crossbows and their bolts; and mounted men who often had their horses armoured and used the spear and the sword. The army also carried baggage carts, tents, drums and metal horns, and the banners, flags and pennons of the command. The siege machines recorded in the History of Sui are background here rather than the scene of this war: the scaling ladders, assault cars, battering rams, the flying towers and the observation turrets were all tools the Sui had already used in the conquest of Chen. This campaign moved back and forth between holding towns and open field, and no record of a large-scale siege belongs to it. Horses were both the base of the cavalry and the source of baggage and of the music of the drums and horns, and the fine horses obtained in dealings with the western frontier were likewise counted among the things the court valued.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術主軸，是隋廷用關中精騎的機動作戰去對付楊諒以人數取勝的烏合之眾。虎牢一役，韋雲起不與叛軍硬拼城垣，而以精騎掩其不意、乘勝直取懷州，把楊諒伸向關中的觸角一次切斷；接著在陝縣方向，他設疑兵，以空旗鼓虛張聲勢於險要處，使敵不敢逼近，而另遣精騎繞擊其後路，叛軍因而被釘在潼關、崤函這條窄道上，河北與關中兩斷，這一連串動作前後不過十數日。淵水之戰的關鍵在「夜」與「疲」兩字：楊諒眾雖多，十餘萬人卻擠在鞏縣一帶的河谷裡，營壘與隊列拉得很長，糧食供應與傳令都不順；王世充率諸軍逼近後沒有立刻強攻，而是等其日久疲弊、陣形鬆散之際乘夜掩擊，騎兵與輕甲步兵同時發動，鼓角聲起，叛軍在黑暗中無從結陣，潰兵互相踐踏，又爭先下水渡河，整個十餘萬的兵眾在一夜之間散盡。追擊由騎兵完成，隋軍一路追出，徑抵城陽。從整體看，隋軍的戰術是分進合擊、各個擊破，而叛軍的失誤則在於把十餘萬人擠在一條河谷裡，指望用人數取勝。
tacticsEn: The tactical axis of this war was the use of the mobile Guanzhong cavalry against a host of Yang Liang that hoped to win by numbers. At Hulao, Wei Yunqi did not grind away at the rebel walls but took the elite cavalry by surprise and pushed on to take Huazhou, cutting off at one stroke the arm that Yang Liang had stretched out towards Guanzhong; then, in the direction of Shanxian, he posted false dispositions, making empty banners and drums at the defile so that the enemy would not dare press forward, while he sent the elite cavalry round to strike their rear. The rebels were thereby nailed to the narrow road of Tongguan and the Hangu passes, and Hebei and Guanzhong were cut apart from each other; the whole sequence of moves took a dozen days or so. The key to the battle of Yuanshui lay in the two words night and weariness. Yang Liang's host was large, but a hundred thousand men or more were pressed into the river valley around Gongxian, their camp and their ranks stretched out over a long front, and neither the food supply nor the chain of command worked smoothly. Wang Shichong, leading the several armies, closed in but did not attack at once; he waited until the rebels were worn out, their formation slackened, and then struck by night. Cavalry and light infantry went forward together, the drums and horns sounded, and the rebels, unable to form up in the darkness, trampled one another and fought to reach the water, so that the whole host of more than a hundred thousand was scattered in a single night. The pursuit was carried out by the cavalry, and the Sui troops followed them through to Chengyang. Taken as a whole, the Sui method was to advance by separate lines and to destroy the enemy in detail, whereas the rebels' mistake was to crowd a hundred thousand men into one river valley in the hope of winning on numbers.
data: 留下數字的地方主要在《隋書·楊諒傳》與《資治通鑑》卷一百八十二，但幾乎都是概數，讀史時不宜當成實帳。兵員方面，楊諒起兵時聚眾十餘萬，通鑑說得一戰之間「十餘萬一朝潰散」；這十餘萬包括河北各州郡徵來的鄉兵、招集的亡命與隨軍家屬，編組鬆散。隋軍的數字史冊只寫「率諸軍」，沒有留下確切總數，能確定的是以關中宿衛與府兵為骨幹，加上河南各州郡的部隊，總量與叛軍不在同一個級別。時間上，從開皇四年春末起兵到十一月淵水決戰，前後約半年，淵水一戰決定全局。地理上，叛軍樞紐並州距洛陽約八百里，關中一路自長安出潼關，潼關至洛陽約二百餘里，虎牢在洛陽東南不足百里，陝縣正當這條線的咽喉；決戰地淵水在鞏縣一帶，位於汜水與洛水之間，距洛陽西南不足百里。物資方面，軍糧由洛陽倉儲與河南州縣供應，朝廷一度蠲免河南租賦以濟軍用；弓矢與槊耗於一夜之間的猛攻，而輜重、鼓吹與車輛盡為隋軍所獲。楊諒被擒時僅與諸子數十人隨行，可見十餘萬眾散盡之速。傷亡數字史無明文，記錄只說追至城陽、河水與泥途阻滯逃散，不可以據以推算。
dataEn: The figures that survive are found mainly in the biography of Yang Liang in the History of Sui and in the hundred and eighty-second juan of the Comprehensive Mirror, but nearly all of them are approximations and should not be read as an audited account. On strength: when Yang Liang rose he gathered a host said to number more than a hundred thousand, and the Mirror says that in a single action more than a hundred thousand were scattered in a single morning; that number covered the militia levies drawn from the prefectures of Hebei, the fugitives he gathered, and the families that followed the army, all of them loosely organised. For the Sui force the histories simply say that Wang Shichong led the several armies and give no exact total; what can be established is that the imperial guards of Guanzhong and the fubing militia formed the backbone, with additional contingents from the prefectures of Henan, so that the two armies were not in the same order of magnitude. In time: from the rising in the late spring of 604 to the decision at Yuanshui in the eleventh month, about half a year elapsed, and the single battle of Yuanshui settled the whole affair. In geography: the rebel base at Bingzhou lies about eight hundred li from Luoyang; the Guanzhong column went out from Chang'an through Tongguan, the road from Tongguan to Luoyang running a little over two hundred li, with Hulao less than a hundred li to the southeast of Luoyang and Shanxian standing exactly on the throat of that line. The field of decision, Yuanshui, lay in the neighbourhood of Gongxian, between the Si River and the Luo River, less than a hundred li southwest of Luoyang. On supply: the grain came from the depots of Luoyang and from the prefectures of Henan, and the court at one point remitted the land tax of Henan to keep the army in the field; bows, arrows and spears were consumed in the ferocity of a single night, while the baggage, the drums and horns and the wagons all fell to the Sui. When Yang Liang was taken he had with him only his sons and a few tens of men, which shows how quickly the host of more than a hundred thousand came apart. Casualty figures are not given: the record says only that the pursuit continued to Chengyang and that the water and the muddy tracks slowed the fugitives, and no computation should be built on it.
cause: 打起來的原因是三層疊在一起。第一層是皇位交接本身帶來的權力真空：隋文帝晚年廢太子楊勇、立晉王楊廣，兄弟之間的信任由此崩解，而文帝又對諸子屢加責罰，把並州、河北、益州幾個要地分給自己的兒子，等於在剛統一的國家內部埋下幾處握有兵權的支點。楊諒、楊秀、楊俊恰好各自鎮守一方，又都對弟弟的即位心懷不滿；文帝病重之際召諸子入宮侍疾，楊諒與楊秀逗留在外而不得入，猜疑由此加深。第二層是並州與河北本身的軍政條件：並州是北方軍事的重心，府兵與邊軍的家戶集中在關中與並州一帶，楊諒以並州總管兼掌河北軍政，徵召容易、聲應者眾，一起兵就能拉出十餘萬人；河北地方勢力把一場宗室內亂當作可以投注的政治資源，隋朝新立、在地方尚未建立牢固的官府秩序，也讓叛軍有了可乘之機。第三層是外交層面的變數：楊諒遣使結好突厥，約以北方之力為外援，隋廷必須在援軍真的到來之前解決他；楊諒也曾一再遣使請罪求和、願意接受改過，隋廷拒絕和議，才把事情推到兵戎相見。
causeEn: Three layers of cause lie on top of one another. The first is the power vacuum that came with the transfer of the throne itself: in his last years Emperor Wen deposed the heir Yang Yong and installed the Prince of Jin, Yang Guang, and the trust between brothers collapsed with that act, while the emperor repeatedly reproached his sons and entrusted the key posts of Bingzhou, of Hebei and of Yizhou to his own sons, which planted in the interior of a freshly unified state several points of military authority. Yang Liang, Yang Xiu and Yang Jun happened to hold one apiece, and all three were displeased at their brother's accession; when Emperor Wen lay dying and summoned his sons to attend him, Yang Liang and Yang Xiu delayed outside and were not admitted, and the suspicion deepened. The second layer lies in the military and administrative conditions of Bingzhou and Hebei themselves. Bingzhou was the weight of the northern frontier, the households of the fubing and of the frontier troops were concentrated in the Guanzhong and Bingzhou regions, and Yang Liang, as Bingzhou commander holding authority over Hebei as well, could call men easily and find many who answered, so that he could raise a host of more than a hundred thousand almost at once. The local forces of Hebei treated a princely civil war as a political stake worth playing for, and the Sui, newly established and not yet endowed with a firm administrative order in the localities, left the rebels an opening. The third layer is the diplomatic variable. Yang Liang sent envoys to the Türkish steppe and promised himself the help of the north, and the Sui court had to settle him before any such help could arrive. Yang Liang also sent envors more than once to confess his fault and sue for peace, ready to be admonished and to mend his ways; it was the refusal of a negotiated settlement that pushed the matter to open war.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果，超出戰場本身。第一，它替新即位的隋主除掉了最直接的內部威脅：楊諒削爵為庶人、幽於益州，益州王楊秀被牽連下獄，襄王楊俊罷官削職，隋室宗親從此再無一方握兵，隋朝得以把全部力量對外。第二，它確立了隋朝此後的基本國策：以關中宿衛與府兵為國力根基，以行軍總管制分路用兵，以洛陽為控制河北與山東的樞紐。楊廣由此看到單靠宗室封藩無法安定天下，反而需要把兵權進一步收歸皇帝與中央官署，這條路後來通向了他的親征高句麗。第三，它留下的隱憂更值得留意：府兵久居京畿、久戰之後兵源凋敝，河北地方武力被削平，隋廷對外用兵時只能臨時徵發天下兵馬，導致大業年間三征高句麗把民力耗盡，隋末的崩潰因此提早。史料上，《隋書·楊諒傳》與《資治通鑑》卷一百八十二是本役的主要依據，而淵水之戰本身沒有獨立的戰史或專門記錄，細節多靠史書轉述，通鑑所引魏徵對國史的補記尤其關鍵。
impactEn: The consequences of this war reach well beyond the battlefield. First, it removed for the newly enthroned sovereign the most immediate internal threat: Yang Liang was stripped of his title and reduced to a commoner and shut up in Yizhou, the Prince of Yizhou, Yang Xiu, was implicated and imprisoned, the Prince of Xiang, Yang Jun, was dismissed and stripped of his offices, and from that day no member of the Sui clan again held troops, so that the dynasty could direct its whole strength outwards. Second, it fixed the basic policy the Sui would follow: the imperial guards of Guanzhong and the fubing militia as the foundation of national strength, the office of xingjun zongguan for dividing an expedition into separate lines, and Luoyang as the hinge for holding Hebei and Shandong. Yang Guang saw from it that appanages alone could not settle the empire, and that the power of the sword had to be gathered still further into the hands of the emperor and the central offices; that road later led to his personal campaigns against Goguryeo. Third, the hidden cost is worth dwelling on. The fubing sat in the capital region for a long time and their numbers thinned out with long service, the local military strength of Hebei was flattened, and when the court fought abroad it could only levy men from all over the empire on the spur of the moment, which is why the three campaigns against Goguryeo in the Daye years drained the people and hastened the collapse of the Sui at the end of the dynasty. As for the sources, the biography of Yang Liang in the History of Sui and the hundred and eighty-second juan of the Comprehensive Mirror are the principal authorities; the battle of Yuanshui has no independent chronicle of its own, and its details survive only through the transmission of the dynastic histories, with the supplementary notes Wei Zheng contributed to the national history, as quoted in the Mirror, being especially important.
result: 結局是楊諒聯軍的徹底瓦解。開皇四年（604）十一月，兩軍戰於鞏縣淵水，隋軍乘夜掩擊，楊諒所聚十餘萬眾一朝散盡，營壘、輜重與鼓吹器械盡為隋軍所收；楊諒本人與諸子數十人逃奔城陽，偽遣使請降，實欲北走突厥，被追騎擒獲，押送洛陽。河北餘下的城邑隨後接連歸降，楊諒被削去秦王封號改為庶人，幽禁於益州；據《隋書》，隋廷在詔令中把楊諒說成是受群下脅迫而反、罪在屬吏，所以不曾族誅，他的兄弟楊秀、楊俊也分別被幽囚與貶職，但楊諒仍逃不掉那十年的囚禁，大業十年（614）卒於益州，年五十有四。從隋朝的角度，這是一場完勝：即位才兩個月的皇帝平掉了唯一能號召河北的宗室，軍隊的編制、調度與後勤在半年間被完整檢驗了一次，隋朝得以用這支部隊去面對高句麗與吐谷渾。從楊諒一方看，則是一場從計畫到崩潰都寫在史書裡的反叛教材：號召得到十餘萬人，卻敗在一夜的疲弊與一次夜襲之上。
resultEn: The outcome was the total disintegration of Yang Liang's coalition. In the eleventh month of 604 the two armies met at Yuanshui near Gongxian; the Sui struck by night, and the host of more than a hundred thousand that Yang Liang had gathered was scattered in a single morning, the camp, the baggage and the drums and horns of the rebels falling entirely into the hands of the victors. Yang Liang himself, with his sons and a few tens of men, fled to Chengyang, sent a false envoy to offer submission in the hope of reaching the Türkish steppe, was caught by the pursuing cavalry and carried off to Luoyang. The remaining cities of Hebei then surrendered one after another. Yang Liang was stripped of the title Prince of Qin and reduced to a commoner, and was shut up in Yizhou; according to the History of Sui, the court declared in its edicts that Yang Liang had been coerced by the men around him and that the guilt lay with his subordinates, so that he was not put to death, while his brothers Yang Xiu and Yang Jun were respectively imprisoned and demoted. Yang Liang nonetheless did not escape the ten years of his imprisonment: he died in Yizhou in the tenth year of the Daye era, 614, at the age of fifty-four. From the point of view of the Sui this was a complete victory. An emperor two months into his reign had destroyed the only member of the imperial clan who could call Hebei to arms, the organisation, the command and the supply of the army had been tested in full over half a year, and the dynasty was left with that army to face Goguryeo and the Tuyuhun. From Yang Liang's side it is a casebook of a rebellion written down from the first plan to the final collapse: a summons that produced more than a hundred thousand men, defeated by a single night of weariness and one surprise attack.
